title: capacity slope fast-probe notes (field) - zainab
summary: Quick scratchpad for a fast linear ramp probe to find the throughput slope and early cliff behavior (short runs, multiple seeds).
content:
Objective:
- Fast-probe a single-model serving pool to characterize the 'capacity slope': how p99 and error-rate evolve when QPS is ramped quickly (60s-600s ramps) versus very-fast probes (30s). Want to detect early cliff and oscillatory desyncs that longer ramps hide.

Test bed:
- Model: redwood-open-7b-quant (v2024-11-21 build)
- Fleet: dev-dedicated-pool-a (4x A10G, 16GB KV each)
- Runtime: release/2024-11-28 w/ continuous-batching=on, prefix-cache=enabled
- Client: local loadgen (k6 harness shim), 100ms think time baseline for multi-sample requests

Configs tried (not exhaustive):
- probe-A (fast): linear ramp 10 -> 800 qps over 60s, hold 30s, teardown
- probe-B (medium): linear ramp 10 -> 800 qps over 300s, hold 60s, teardown
- probe-C (burst): staircase 10->200->400->800 each step 30s, with 5s microbursts + noise 20%
- concurrency cap: 64 per worker
- batching target: prefer tokens-per-batch 4096, max-batch-wait 12ms

Metrics collected (per run): p50/p90/p99 latency (ms), tail errors (5xx), queue depth, avg batch size, KV cache hit rate, tokens/sec, GPU util.%

Representative observations:
- probe-A (60s ramp): p50 stayed under 120ms up to ~420 qps. p99 has a sharp knee at ~430-470 qps and jumps from ~350ms -> ~1.3s within 20s of the knee. Error-rate (502/503) remained low until 520 qps, then sporadic spikes coincident with queue depth surges.
- probe-B (300s ramp): knee smoothed out and appeared ~470 qps, p99 rose gradually to 600ms by 600 qps. No large error bursts. Suggests that slower ramps allow autoscaler/batching to adapt, avoiding transient queue blowups.
- probe-C (staircase + microbursts): system showed resonant oscillation: a microburst stepping to 400 qps caused queue depth to climb, autoscaler reacted but lagged; on step to 800 qps we saw repeated p99 spikes and CPU-side thread stalls (observed via application thread dump).

Quick ascii sketch (probe-A p99 vs qps timeline):
- time 0s: qps=10 p99~90ms
- time 30s: qps~200 p99~180ms
- time 52s: qps~450 p99~400ms (start knee)
- time 58s: qps~520 p99~1.3s (cliff)

Insights / hypotheses:
1) Fast ramps reveal a dynamic mismatch between batch formation latency and the autoscaler/capacity soft-limiting. The runtime doesn't have enough time to increase average batch sizes (or to leverage KV priming), so per-token CPU overhead dominates causing the p99 cliff.
2) Slower ramps give batching and the admission controller time to coalesce requests; the visible knee shifts higher and is less steep.
3) Microbursts interact poorly with current concurrency cappings; there is a 'resonant window' where burst frequency aligns with batch-formation windows producing sustained high queue depth.
4) Some thread scheduling stalls observed when switching from moderate to high qps quickly — look at GC/Python GIL and python worker queue scheduling.

Immediate next experiments (short list):
- Repeat probe-A with increased max-batch-wait from 12ms -> 25ms to see if larger batches preempt the cliff.
- Run probe-A with prefix-cache primed vs cold (toggle to measure cache priming effect).
- Enable a conservative admission backoff (soft cap at 70% util) and re-run fast ramp to see if graceful backpressure flatten the cliff.
- Add short-run systemprofiling (perf + flamegraph) around the knee to capture thread stalls.

Notes to self:
- Save full run traces and slice around p99 jumps: traces/2024-12-03/cap-slope-fastprobe.zip (linked in GH PR).
- Check linked GH issue for earlier similar regression (redwood/serve#778) — may share patterns.
- Share a short writeup for Eng-runtime weekly (1 slide + 3 bullet TL;DR).

Conclusion (quick):
- Fast probes are valuable to surface transient cliffs and resonant oscillations that longer ramps hide. For capacity planning, we should combine both fast probes (catch brittle spots) + slower ramps (estimate sustainable throughput).

Timestamped logs and raw metrics: see linked_artifacts; I'll attach CSV snippets to PR after cleaning.

-- Zainab

Unresolved questions:
- Is the observed thread stall pattern reproducible on A100-based pools? (schedule a quick A100 micro-run.)
- Does per-tenant variance shift the knee left/right? Try single-tenant vs mixed-tenant runs.
